paragraphs.source_en:
Maeve the great queen was pacing to and fro,
Between the walls covered with beaten bronze, 10
In her high house at Cruachan 1 ; the long hearth,
Flickering with ash and hazel, but half showed
Where the tired horse-boys lay upon the rushes,
Or on the benches underneath the walls,
In comfortable sleep; all living slept
But that great queen, who more than half the night
Had paced from door to fire and fire to door.
 Though now in her old age, in her young age
She had been beautiful in that old way
That's all but gone; for the proud heart is gone, 20
And the fool heart of the counting-house fears all
But soft beauty and indolent desire.
 She could have called over the rim of the world
Whatever woman's lover had hit her fancy,
And yet had been great-bodied and great-limbed,
Fashioned to be the mother of strong children;
And she'd had lucky eyes and a high heart,
And wisdom that caught fire like the dried flax,
